title: ESJ fixture manifest
description: A file of the fixture manifest: the core manifest, one part of it, or the rule case file the core manifest names in rules.casesFile. The core manifest and a part have the same shape; a part carries the fixtures of one edition and is left out of a distribution that does not ship that edition. A rule case file carries its pack, the directory of that pack and the cases, and names no part.

format.description: The kind of file. A rule case file says -Rules.

version.description: The version of the fixture contract, raised when a member changes meaning.

part.description: In a manifest file, core or the name of the edition part.

specification.description: The specification the fixtures are of, relative to the repository root.

parts.description: Further manifest files, beside this one. A part that is not in the distribution is not an error: it is an edition this distribution does not carry.

semanticModel.description: The edition a part belongs to, as a document names it.

whenEditionAbsent.description: The finding an implementation that does not carry this edition reports instead of evaluating L2 and L3.

registries.description: The registries to load before anything else in this file is run.

documents.description: Documents that are conformant, unless a findings member says otherwise.

invalid.description: Documents that must be rejected, with the layer and the code.

canonicalOrder.description: Documents whose members are written in the wrong order, with the bytes a canonicalizer has to produce.

grammars.description: The value grammars of the specification, section 6, as accept and reject tables.

rules.description: Where the rule pack and its cases are.

arithmetic.description: A pack of the rule language whose rules pin its arithmetic, the document it is run over, and what it reports there.

pack.description: In a rule case file, the pack the cases are evaluated with.

directory.description: In a rule case file, the directory of that pack, relative to the repository root.

cases.description: In a rule case file, the cases themselves.

path.description: A semantic path of the specification, section 5.1.

code.description: A finding code of the specification, section 9.6.

value.description: A value as a document writes it: a string, or the object of the specification, section 6.1.

max.description: A number, or n where the registry writes n.

file.description: The document in pretty form, relative to the repository root.

canonical.description: The canonical bytes, where the repository carries them. Where it does not, documentDigest is what pins them.

registries.description: The registry files this document was measured with, the core registry of its edition first. An implementation that carries fewer of them measures other terms than the manifest records.

findings.description: The errors layers L2 and L3 report, in the order a validator reports them. Absent means none.

subject.description: What the finding is about where the path cannot name it.

layer.description: The layer that catches the defect. limit is a configured bound and not a defect of the document; business-rule is a document no layer of this specification rejects.

base.description: The document a candidate is substituted into.

rule.description: The rule the case is aimed at, empty for a near miss.

base.description: The conformant document the changes are applied to.

pack.description: The pack, relative to the repository root. Its rules are written in the rule language alone: no rule written in code, no code list snapshot.

base.description: The document the pack is run over. No rule of the pack reads a business term of it; it names the edition the pack is compiled against.

rules.description: Every rule identifier the pack reports, sorted.

warnings.description: The subset whose findings decide no verdict.
